gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-003 identifies the same Algorithm 2 defect: the distance d is an angle with extremal value arccos(1/sqrt(n)), but both threshold tests compare it to 1/sqrt(n), causing incorrect rejection and acceptance classifications. Its specific repair changes both thresholds to the angular target or consistently redefines the target function.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: Algorithm 2 uses thresholds on the wrong mathematical scale, confusing the angle arccos(1/sqrt(n)) with its cosine 1/sqrt(n) in both extremality tests.

component_coverage.gold_component: Both Algorithm 2 threshold predicates are centered at 1/sqrt(n) even though d and the conjectured extremal value are angular, so extremal and nonextremal candidates can be misclassified.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction explicitly states that d is an angle, the tests use the cosine 1/sqrt(n), derives the resulting rejection of extremal subspaces, and prescribes correcting both thresholds to arccos(1/sqrt(n)) ± epsilon or making the definition consistently cosine-valued.
